\begin{abstract}
Do demographic personas improve an LLM's prediction of audience engagement? We compare a fixed
ten-persona panel with a generic-reader baseline on Upworthy headlines, with supplementary archived
news and Reddit comparisons. The primary experiment collects Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite and GPT-4.1
observations on the same \newSelectedN{}-package exploratory cohort, selected with simultaneous
winner screening. It allocates thirty scores per arm and variant within model, retains exact raw
responses, and reports metric-specific valid and paired counts. Complete-package coverage is
\newGeminiN{} for Gemini and \newGptN{} for GPT-4.1. The baseline-minus-panel Kendall $\tau_b$ gap is
\newGeminiGapTau{} (CI [\newGeminiGapTauLow{}, \newGeminiGapTauHigh{}]) for Gemini and
\newGptGapTau{} (CI [\newGptGapTauLow{}, \newGptGapTauHigh{}]) for GPT-4.1, on respectively
\newGeminiPairedTauN{} and \newGptPairedTauN{} valid rank pairs. Expected top-1 is
\newGeminiPanelTopOne{} versus \newGeminiBaselineTopOne{} for Gemini and \newGptPanelTopOne{}
versus \newGptBaselineTopOne{} for GPT-4.1 (panel versus baseline). These intervals condition on
the selected cohort and recorded generations. The Upworthy archive documents a randomization-risk
period. Excluding that period in a post-hoc sensitivity retains positive expected top-1 and lift
gaps in both configurations, while Gemini tau-b and Spearman intervals include zero. Archived
Reddit top-1 and captured lift favor the panel, so the direction of the comparison depends on
dataset and metric. A raw-replay artifact supports offline reproduction of the primary experiment.
The results concern this panel, cohort, and protocol; they are not a new held-out evaluation or
evidence of universal persona harm. Provider request protocols differ across models, and no
causal mechanism is isolated.
\end{abstract}

\paragraph{Metric identity.}
For concordant and discordant pair counts $C,D$, Goodman--Kruskal gamma is
\[
\gamma=(C-D)/(C+D),
\]
discarding pairs tied in either variable~\citep{goodman1954}. It is undefined when $C+D=0$ and
differs from Kendall $\tau_b$, which accounts for ties:
\[
\tau_b=\frac{C-D}{\sqrt{(C+D+T_x)(C+D+T_y)}},
\]
where $T_x,T_y$ count pairs tied only in the respective variable~\citep{kendall1945ties}.
Spearman uses average ranks~\citep{spearman1904}. Constant rank inputs yield undefined values.

\paragraph{Elicitation and aggregation.}
The prompt requests JSON with a \texttt{click\_intent} number in $[0,1]$
(Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix}). Scores are averaged across recorded observations:
\[
\widehat{s}(v)=\frac{1}{|O_v|}\sum_{(i,d)\in O_v}y_{i,d}(v).
\]
With complete draws this equals the mean over personas and draws. With missing draws it can
differ from the historical H5 mean, which weights draw-collapsed personas equally. The supplementary aggregation comparison evaluates these alternative rules.

\paragraph{Archived winner screen.}
The archived aggregate comparisons use the observed best variant and runner-up. The procedure chose the observed best variant and compared it with the observed runner-up
using a one-sided pooled two-proportion $z$ test at $p<0.05$, selecting \legacySelectedN{} packages.
The direction was chosen from the data: even a two-arm null comparison can pass in either
direction, so the nominal one-sided threshold does not imply a five-percent false-positive rate.
Comparing only the runner-up need not separate a winner from every opponent. Outcome selection
changes the evaluation population. Packages failing a screen are not thereby unpredictable.

\paragraph{Simultaneous winner screen.}
The primary experiment requires a unique observed maximum and compares it with every opponent using
two-sided pooled $z$ tests. For $k$ variants the comparison family contains $m=k(k-1)/2$ unordered
pairs. All winner--opponent comparisons must pass $\alpha/m$, with $\alpha=0.05$.
The screening statistic is $\min(1,m\max_{j\ne w}p_{wj})$. Bonferroni's inequality motivates the
adjustment~\citep{nistBonferroni}. The nominal bound is approximate and per package, conditional on
independent binomial observations and adequate normal approximation. It is not an across-package
false-discovery guarantee or proof of a population winner. Repeated exposures and Reddit voting
further limit these assumptions. In the restored corpus \newSelectedN{} packages pass, all within
the historical selected set. A stricter screen does not demonstrate that removed packages had
false winners.

\section{Discussion and Limitations}
The comparisons make a generic-reader baseline necessary for this task. A persona panel adds
assumptions about audience composition and behavior that require predictive validation.
The new matched-score comparisons favor the baseline in valid rank comparisons, expected top-1
and captured lift, but do not establish a bottom-1 advantage. Gemini rank means exclude constant
outputs with explicit arm-specific counts; top-1 retains those packages through expected tie
credit. Historical Upworthy reports and the scalar GPT diagnostic also favor the baseline;
historical Reddit decision metrics favor the panel. Excluding the documented randomization-risk
period preserves the new top-1 and lift contrasts but leaves Gemini tau-b and Spearman uncertain.
The ranking conclusion therefore depends on cohort and estimator, not just model configuration.
